purpose: Supplemental researched macro fingerprints for tracked names that were missing from the legacy macro-sensitivities file or need current-holding aliases. Loaded after the base file; same-ticker entries intentionally override the base profile.
methodology: Macro profiles describe economic sensitivity, not fundamental quality and not a buy/sell score. Factor weights are normalized near 1.00; sensitivities are -5 to +5. Only channels present in the current macro-context participate in the live adjustment.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.profileNote: Current earnings still come mainly from autos and energy storage; market sensitivity is unusually high because autonomy/Optimus optionality is capitalised far ahead of cash flows.

industrialCapex.rationale: Grid-scale storage and manufacturing expansion benefit from power/industrial capex.

financialConditions.rationale: Long-duration autonomy/robotics expectations make the equity highly sensitive to real yields and discount rates.

riskAppetite.rationale: Narrative optionality and a premium multiple amplify changes in speculative appetite.

consumerStrength.rationale: Vehicle demand and financing affordability remain exposed to household strength.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Battery metals, electronics and logistics inflation can pressure vehicle and storage margins.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower expected rates improve auto affordability and duration valuation.

growthDemand.rationale: Broad growth supports vehicle, energy and automation demand.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Tesla's balance sheet is strong, but weak-end credit stress usually compresses premium-growth multiples and auto financing demand.

stocks.derivedFrom: Current Power Stack holdings/robotics research and Sep 2 macro regime.

stocks.name: Symbotic
stocks.profileNote: Commercial warehouse automation with real deployments; materially less dependent on humanoid adoption but still duration-sensitive.

industrialCapex.rationale: Warehouse automation budgets and deployment cadence are the primary demand channel.

financialConditions.rationale: Higher real yields pressure growth multiples and customer capex hurdle rates.

riskAppetite.rationale: High-growth automation equities rerate with risk appetite.

labourStrength.rationale: Labour scarcity/wage pressure improves automation ROI; an abundant cheap-labour backdrop weakens urgency.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Electronics/mechanical inflation can pressure project margins.

policyRelief.rationale: Easier expected policy helps duration valuation.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Weak credit can defer customer expansion and compress high-growth multiples.

stocks.derivedFrom: Power Stack robotics research; commercial-deployment hierarchy.

stocks.name: Cognex
stocks.profileNote: Machine vision is a mature enabling layer for factory and warehouse automation with better current-economics visibility than humanoid exposure.

industrialCapex.rationale: Factory automation and machine-vision capex drive demand.

growthDemand.rationale: Industrial and electronics production cycles affect orders.

financialConditions.rationale: Rates mainly affect valuation and customer capex rather than solvency.

riskAppetite.rationale: Automation multiple expands/contracts with growth appetite.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Component inflation and shortages can pressure margins/delivery.

labourStrength.rationale: Labour scarcity raises the ROI of automation.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Credit stress can delay smaller industrial customers' capex.

stocks.name: Teradyne
stocks.profileNote: Semiconductor-test cyclicality plus collaborative/mobile robotics exposure makes industrial capex and electronics demand the dominant macro channels.

industrialCapex.rationale: Semiconductor test and automation orders follow capex cycles.

growthDemand.rationale: Electronics/semiconductor demand drives test utilisation and orders.

riskAppetite.rationale: Semiconductor and robotics valuation responds to growth appetite.

financialConditions.rationale: Higher real yields pressure semiconductor growth multiples.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Component constraints can affect margins and deliveries.

policyRelief.rationale: Easier expected rates help duration valuation.

labourStrength.rationale: Labour scarcity modestly supports automation ROI.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Credit stress weakens cyclical capex appetite.

stocks.derivedFrom: Power Stack robotics and semiconductor-test research.

stocks.name: Geekplus
stocks.profileNote: Warehouse AMR exposure has a clearer adoption path than humanoids, but the equity remains young and sensitive to China/global capex and risk appetite.

industrialCapex.rationale: Warehouse automation budgets are the core demand driver.

financialConditions.rationale: Young growth equity is sensitive to discount rates and expansion funding.

riskAppetite.rationale: Post-IPO valuation is highly sentiment sensitive.

consumerStrength.rationale: Retail/e-commerce volumes influence customer automation ROI.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Electronics, motors and logistics inflation can pressure hardware margins.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Funding/customer-capex risk rises when weak credit deteriorates.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower rates modestly help valuation and capex.

stocks.name: UBTECH Robotics
stocks.profileNote: Industrial humanoid optionality remains pre-scale relative to conventional automation; financing and risk appetite dominate the equity response.

industrialCapex.rationale: Factory deployment budgets are necessary for commercialisation.

financialConditions.rationale: Long-duration, capital-intensive commercialisation is highly rate sensitive.

riskAppetite.rationale: Humanoid narrative exposure is highly sentiment driven.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Actuators, reducers, electronics and batteries are cost-sensitive inputs.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Funding-dependent concept equities are especially vulnerable to weak-credit stress.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower expected rates support duration valuation.

labourStrength.rationale: Labour scarcity can improve the long-run automation case but is not the near-term earnings driver.

stocks.name: SLB
stocks.profileNote: Oilfield-services cash flow remains tied to upstream spending, while the Kelvion transaction adds a growing data-centre thermal-management crossover.

crudeTightness.rationale: Sustained crude strength supports customer upstream budgets and service intensity.

industrialCapex.rationale: Upstream, energy-infrastructure and data-centre cooling investment support orders.

growthDemand.rationale: Global activity affects oil demand and producer spending.

gasTightness.rationale: Gas/LNG investment supports international service activity.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Labour/equipment/logistics inflation can pressure service margins.

financialConditions.rationale: Rates affect customer project economics and acquisition financing.

productTightness.rationale: Refined-product tightness can indirectly sustain upstream/refinery spending but is not the primary earnings channel.

riskAppetite.rationale: Energy-equity multiples respond modestly to risk appetite.

labourStrength.rationale: Tight skilled labour raises service costs.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Weak producer/project financing can reduce marginal activity.

stocks.derivedFrom: Power Stack oil-services and Sep 1 SLB/Kelvion research.

stocks.name: Marathon Petroleum
stocks.profileNote: Refining economics are driven more by product cracks and utilisation than flat crude direction; current product scarcity is the key macro channel.

productTightness.rationale: Diesel/gasoline/jet crack strength directly supports refining margins.

growthDemand.rationale: Transport and industrial demand support product volumes.

crudeTightness.rationale: Crude spikes can raise feedstock cost unless product cracks widen faster.

consumerStrength.rationale: Driving/fuel demand has a consumer component.

financialConditions.rationale: Balance-sheet sensitivity is modest relative to margin cycles.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Non-crude operating and maintenance inflation can pressure margins.

riskAppetite.rationale: Cyclical energy multiples respond modestly to risk appetite.

policyRelief.rationale: Rates matter less than physical product balances.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Stress mainly affects valuation/demand at the margin.

stocks.name: Valero Energy
stocks.profileNote: High-quality refining beta: product tightness is the dominant positive channel, while crude-only spikes without demand resilience can be adverse.

productTightness.rationale: Middle-distillate and gasoline cracks are the core earnings transmission.

growthDemand.rationale: Fuel volumes depend on transport/industrial activity.

crudeTightness.rationale: Feedstock spikes are adverse if product prices do not keep pace.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Operating-cost inflation can pressure throughput economics.

riskAppetite.rationale: Energy multiple modestly follows risk appetite.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Stress mainly works through end demand and valuation.

policyRelief.rationale: Physical product balance dominates monetary-policy sensitivity.

stocks.name: Enphase Energy
stocks.profileNote: Turnaround solar/storage exposure is highly sensitive to financing costs and housing demand; power scarcity helps but does not override residential-rate sensitivity.

financialConditions.rationale: Residential solar/storage economics are highly sensitive to borrowing costs.

housingStrength.rationale: Residential installations correlate with housing/household investment activity.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower expected rates improve project economics and growth valuation.

consumerStrength.rationale: Household balance sheets affect discretionary energy upgrades.

industrialCapex.rationale: Storage/electrification demand benefits from broader power investment, though residential remains primary.

riskAppetite.rationale: Turnaround clean-tech multiples are sentiment sensitive.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Weak consumer/project credit sharply reduces financed installations.

stocks.name: nVent Electric
stocks.profileNote: Electrical distribution and data-centre power infrastructure are structurally advantaged, with acquisition/integration and input costs the main macro-sensitive offsets.

industrialCapex.rationale: Data-centre and electrification capex drive enclosure/power-distribution demand.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Copper/steel/electrical-component inflation can pressure margins without pricing.

financialConditions.rationale: Rates affect customer capex and acquisition economics.

riskAppetite.rationale: AI-infrastructure multiple is partly sentiment driven.

consumerStrength.rationale: Consumer exposure is secondary to industrial/data-centre demand.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Project-credit stress can defer marginal customer builds.

stocks.name: SpaceX
stocks.profileNote: Private/illiquid long-duration optionality; market value is dominated by risk appetite, capital availability and execution rather than near-term public-market fundamentals.

financialConditions.rationale: Large capital requirements and distant cash-flow optionality are highly rate sensitive.

riskAppetite.rationale: Private-market valuation and secondary liquidity depend heavily on speculative appetite.

industrialCapex.rationale: Launch, satellite and infrastructure investment support growth.

growthDemand.rationale: Enterprise/government connectivity demand benefits from economic activity.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower expected rates improve duration/private-market valuation.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Private-capital stress reduces secondary liquidity and funding appetite.

stocks.name: NationGate Holdings
stocks.profileNote: Malaysia AI-server manufacturing exposure has real demand but higher customer-concentration, margin and capex-cycle sensitivity than grid/electrical bottlenecks.

industrialCapex.rationale: AI-server and electronics buildout is the core demand driver.

riskAppetite.rationale: High-beta AI manufacturing valuation is sentiment sensitive.

financialConditions.rationale: Capex funding and valuation respond to rates.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Memory/semiconductor/component inflation can squeeze contract-manufacturing margins.

tailCreditStress.rationale: AI-financing stress can defer customer orders and compress high-beta multiples.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower rates modestly help capex and valuation.

stocks.name: DIALOG Group
stocks.profileNote: Tank terminals, storage and downstream infrastructure provide more fee/infrastructure exposure than pure upstream beta; product/gas flows matter alongside crude.

productTightness.rationale: Tight product markets support storage/logistics utilisation and downstream activity.

crudeTightness.rationale: Higher regional oil flows can support terminal/infrastructure activity.

industrialCapex.rationale: Petrochemical/energy infrastructure projects drive engineering activity.

growthDemand.rationale: Regional industrial demand influences throughput and projects.

financialConditions.rationale: Project economics respond to financing costs.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Construction/material inflation can pressure project margins.

riskAppetite.rationale: Cyclical energy sentiment affects valuation modestly.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Weak project credit can delay marginal developments.

stocks.name: Powerwell Holdings
stocks.profileNote: Small-cap switchboard/power-distribution exposure benefits directly from Malaysia data-centre and grid capex, but input costs and project concentration increase volatility.

industrialCapex.rationale: Data-centre, industrial and electrical-distribution projects are the main demand driver.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Copper/electrical-component inflation can pressure project margins.

financialConditions.rationale: Small-cap/customer project financing is rate sensitive.

riskAppetite.rationale: Small-cap data-centre-theme valuation is sentiment sensitive.

housingStrength.rationale: Construction demand contributes but is secondary to industrial/data-centre projects.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower rates modestly support project finance/valuation.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Small-cap and project-finance sensitivity rises in weak credit.

stocks.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
stocks.profileNote: Mostly idiosyncratic GTA VI/franchise exposure; macro works primarily through consumer demand and the discount rate rather than industrial themes.

consumerStrength.rationale: Premium game spending and engagement benefit from healthy discretionary demand.

financialConditions.rationale: Large future-title cash flows make valuation moderately duration sensitive.

riskAppetite.rationale: Catalyst-heavy growth valuation responds to equity appetite.

growthDemand.rationale: Broad growth supports discretionary entertainment spending.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower expected rates help valuation more than operations.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Labour/development costs matter but are mostly company-specific.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Credit stress mainly transmits via consumer spending and valuation.

stocks.derivedFrom: Current holdings review; GTA VI remains the dominant idiosyncratic catalyst.

stocks.name: MISC Berhad
stocks.profileNote: Shipping/energy-infrastructure cash flows are driven by tanker/LNG rates and contract structure; current transaction/funding risk remains company-specific.

crudeTightness.rationale: Oil rerouting and seaborne flows can tighten tanker utilisation/rates.

gasTightness.rationale: LNG security demand supports shipping/related infrastructure.

productTightness.rationale: Energy-logistics disruption can raise tonne-mile demand, though MISC is not a pure product-tanker play.

financialConditions.rationale: Capital-intensive fleet/project funding is sensitive to yields.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Operating, maintenance and financing costs can pressure returns.

riskAppetite.rationale: Cyclical shipping valuation moves modestly with risk appetite.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Funding stress matters to capital-intensive transactions/projects.

policyRelief.rationale: Lower rates marginally improve funding economics.

stocks.derivedFrom: Current holdings review and energy-logistics thesis.

stocks.name: Dayang Enterprise Holdings
stocks.profileNote: Offshore maintenance/OSV exposure benefits from sustained upstream activity, but utilisation and work-order conversion dominate over spot oil alone.

crudeTightness.rationale: Sustained oil strength supports Malaysian upstream maintenance and offshore activity.

industrialCapex.rationale: Upstream maintenance/capex and work-order awards drive utilisation.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Marine labour, fuel and maintenance inflation pressure margins.

financialConditions.rationale: Fleet/project financing matters, though balance sheet has improved.

productTightness.rationale: Product tightness supports broader energy economics only indirectly.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Weak project/customer credit can delay offshore activity.

policyRelief.rationale: Rates are secondary to utilisation and upstream spending.

stocks.derivedFrom: Current holdings review; weak Q2 execution kept separate from macro sensitivity.

stocks.name: Hibiscus Petroleum
stocks.profileNote: Direct upstream oil beta with improving operating fundamentals; use this alias for the canonical holding while 5199 remains the All-Ideas ticker.

crudeTightness.rationale: Realised oil price is the dominant cash-flow channel.

growthDemand.rationale: Global demand affects oil balance and realised pricing.

industrialCapex.rationale: Development/maintenance spending supports production growth but requires capital discipline.

financialConditions.rationale: Rates affect project economics and valuation.

inputCostPressure.rationale: Offshore service and operating-cost inflation can offset oil-price gains.

riskAppetite.rationale: Small-cap upstream valuation responds to energy risk appetite.

productTightness.rationale: Refined-product scarcity supports crude demand at the margin but is not direct refinery exposure.

tailCreditStress.rationale: Funding stress can compress small-cap cyclicals.

policyRelief.rationale: Monetary policy is secondary to oil and execution.

stocks.derivedFrom: Current holdings review; alias of 5199 for portfolio records.
